is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles coluzzii (a member of the An. gambiae complex) in Anambra State, Nigeria (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr L1014F) and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) (Page 1, Abstract; Page 10, Tables 7 and 8).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 7 and 8 provide genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) and allele frequencies for kdr L1014F and ace-1 G119S for three populations (Page 10).

african_field_population.evidence: Larvae were collected from field sites in Awka, Onitsha, and Nnewi, Anambra State, Nigeria (Page 3, Collection and maintenance of mosquito larvae).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study conducting field collections, bioassays, and molecular analysis (Page 1, Abstract).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is provided for three specific urban centers: Awka, Onitsha, and Nnewi in Anambra State, Nigeria (Page 1, Abstract).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection occurred between September 2024 and August 2025 (Page 3, Collection and maintenance of mosquito larvae).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections conducted between 2024 and 2025.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and bioassay results, are provided in the main text tables.

assessment.summary: This study assessed insecticide resistance in Anopheles coluzzii from three urban centers in Anambra State, Nigeria. It combined WHO tube bioassays with molecular genotyping for kdr L1014F and ace-1 G119S. High resistance to pyrethroids and DDT was observed, associated with high kdr 1014F allele frequencies, while populations remained susceptible to carbamates and organophosphates.
